summary: Amod Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist. She studied at Barnard College, INALCO, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald. She was a visiting instructor at Yale (1982) and is attested at the CNRS in 2005.
Amy L. Mann works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her BA at Scripps College, where she studied under thesis readers and mentors Zhiru Ng and Zayn Kassam.

Amy Paris Langenberg specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (~2002–2008) and served as assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (~2014).

Amy Sims Miller is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Virginia (MA, PhD under David Germano), as well as with Janice Dean Willis and several traditional Tibetan teachers.
Amy Snyder Ohta works in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (1990, 1993), taught Qian Lin, and held a post at the University of Washington (~1995).

Ana Agud is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Salamanca and the University of Tübingen. She served as a professor in the Department of Classical and Indo-European Philology at the University of Salamanca (~1976–2018).

Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He was educated at Royal College, Colombo, and Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, and founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891.

Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He held a doctorate from the University of Freiburg, studied under Tomo Geshe Rinpoche, lectured at Patna University, and served as Ācārya at Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933–1985).
Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and has served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation.

Ananda Coomaraswamy (1877–1947) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at University College London (~1897–1904), he later held posts at the Smithsonian Institution and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (~1917–1947).

Ananda W. P. Guruge (1928–2014) studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of London. An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at NIEPA (attested 1970) and was Dean Emeritus of Academic Affairs at University of the West (~2000–2014).

Anant Sadashiv Altekar (1898–1959) was an Indologist and historian. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), Patna University (~1949–1959), and served as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (~1950–1959).

Anantalal Thakur (1916–2009) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as a professor at Mithila Research Institute (~1955–1974) and as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).
Ananya Jahanara Kabir is a scholar in Indology and other fields. She studied at the University of Cambridge and took up a post at King's College London in ~2013.

Andrea Acri is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Raffaele Torella and completed his PhD at Leiden University under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, joining the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2016.

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University, later becoming Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (~2017–2021).
Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed both her Master's degree (-2008) and her PhD (-2014) at the Free University of Berlin.

Andreas Doctor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and studied under several traditional teachers, including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche.
Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of Bristol under Paul Williams, having also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
